text:
lia: Quick sync — post-1.3 feedback pile is in. We have a clear split: one correctness bug affecting a small percent of requests and a set of low-urgency UX enhancements customers are requesting. Need to decide fix now vs schedule.

trent: Can you surface the numbers? Impacted customers + failure modes?

kyle: Support collected reports: 3 enterprise customers (alpha group) saw occasional label duplication in generated metadata, ~1% of calls during burst tests. Non-blocking in prod but causes their downstream dedupe to fail tests.

anya: The UX asks are more about optional metadata display and templating. High value for adoption but not breaking.

chao: From infra: the duplication looks like a race in the postprocessor when load spikes. Reproducible in staging with long burst workloads. Cost to fix should be small (lock or reorder), low-risk.

lia: So bug is small blast radius but hurts acceptance for a few key accounts. Product tradeoff: hotfix now (pull engineers) vs bundle in next enhancement sprint and offer mitigations. Thoughts?

trent: I vote hotfix. If it's 1% and blocks acceptance for large customers, delaying threatens expansion. Estimate 1 week dev + QA + canary.

anya: If we do hotfix, can we also land a tiny UX improvement as part of the rollout (toggle to show metadata) to soften ask backlog? Small UI change that reduces perception of missing features.

lia: OK that's a middle path. Hotfix for duplication + quick toggle feature. We still need to decide scope for backlog grooming: which UX items go to immediate next sprint vs backlog (Q2).

kyle: From CS perspective, if we ship hotfix in 7 days and enable toggle earlier via config, customers are satisfied. We can offer a temporary workaround in docs: postprocess dedupe step.

trent: Plan: branch hotfix -> run full stress suite -> canary on one Dedicated cluster for 48h -> expand. I can spare two engineers (me + 1) for this week. Put highest priority on tests for race reproduction.

chao: I'll set up the canary pipeline and alerting (stream duplication rate, p95 latency, memory). Add a rollback marker.

pm-bot: Created ticket PROD-6123: postproc-dedupe-hotfix. Assignees: @trent @sophie. Link: https://redwood/tasks/PROD-6123

lia: Acceptance criteria to close: (1) duplication rate <0.1% under burst tests for 72h on canary; (2) no p95 latency regression >100ms; (3) docs updated with workaround.

anya: For grooming: we'll prioritize toggle + one templating small request into next sprint (sprint+1). Rest go into backlog for the roadmap review.

trent: ETA: PR today, canary Tuesday morning.

kyle: I'll notify the affected customers and offer the workaround + an opt-in flag.

lia: Thanks. We'll revisit during the weekly roadmap meeting to slot remaining UX asks into Q2 vs backlog. If hotfix uncovers deeper infra issues we re-evaluate scope. :thumbsup:
